title: Web UI dead in real browsers: ApiClient calls unbound global fetch → Illegal invocation
description:
LIVE BUG (found testing launched app). Overview shows dead/NO SIGNAL state; every /api/* call fails with 'cannot reach the local server' (AppError kind=network) in a real browser, while curl + all vitest tests pass.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed via CDP against the running server): web/src/api/client.ts:137 stores the global fetch UNBOUND — 'this.#fetch = opts.fetchImpl ?? fetch' — and invokes it as 'this.#fetch(url, init)'. In Chrome/Safari/Firefox, window.fetch is this-sensitive: calling it with this=ApiClient instance throws TypeError: Failed to execute 'fetch' on 'Window': Illegal invocation, BEFORE any request is issued (CDP shows zero Network.requestWillBeSent for /api/*). The #get/#send catch maps the TypeError to ApiError(0,'network') → shell renders SIGNAL LOST 'cannot reach the local server'. Node's undici fetch ignores this, so the full test suite and CLI report path never see it.

REPRO: npm run build; node dist/cli/index.js launch --no-open; open the printed URL in Chrome → SIGNAL LOST; devtools console shows Illegal invocation. curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <tok>' http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/report returns 2 agents.

FIX: bind at storage — this.#fetch = opts.fetchImpl ?? fetch.bind(globalThis) (or wrap in an arrow). ONE site; ws/client.ts uses 'new WebSocket' (constructor, not this-sensitive) — clean.

REGRESSION TEST: in client.test, stub a this-sensitive fetch (function that throws unless this===globalThis||this===undefined after bind semantics) as the GLOBAL and construct ApiClient WITHOUT fetchImpl; assert a #get succeeds. Must fail on the unbound form.

VERIFY: rebuild, relaunch, drive real Chrome (headless CDP) → Overview renders CLAUDE-CODE + CODEX SignalStrips, stats agents=2.
acceptance_criteria: ApiClient default fetch is bound/wrapped; unit regression test that fails on unbound form; headless Chrome against launched server renders 2 agent SignalStrips on Overview; tsc/eslint/prettier/vitest green
notes: Fixed unbound browser fetch: web/src/api/client.ts constructor now uses opts.fetchImpl ?? fetch.bind(globalThis) (injected fetchImpl unchanged, comment added). Regression test added in web/src/api/client.test.ts: 'ApiClient default fetch binding > calls the global fetch with globalThis as `this` (browser fetch is this-sensitive)' using vi.stubGlobal + vi.unstubAllGlobals; verified it FAILS (ApiError status 0 network, 'Illegal invocation') on the unbound form and passes with the fix. Gates (direct binaries): tsc --noEmit clean; eslint client.ts+client.test.ts clean; prettier --check src/** web/src/** clean; vitest run web/src/api = 2 files / 32 tests passed. Not committed (orchestrator commits).
close_reason: Fixed in b0b1782: default fetch bound to globalThis (client.ts); regression test fails on unbound form; adversarial review APPROVE (bug-class sweep of web/src found no other this-sensitive stored globals); verified live in headless Chrome via CDP — Overview renders 2 AGENTS (CLAUDE-CODE + CODEX SignalStrips), all /api/* 200. Full gates green: tsc, eslint, prettier, vitest 1743/1743.

title: Server: structured hook add/remove op — raw-on-server edit, redacted diff, project+global
description:
User decision 2026-07-28: the tool manages agent config, so global entries must be editable — with a warning. This bead is the hooks slice of wmc.11's structured-write concept: server-side surgical edits so a redacted settings.json can be modified WITHOUT the client round-tripping redacted content (the redaction save trap; the user's real ~/.claude/settings.json has an env block and IS redacted).

ENDPOINT: POST /api/hooks/edit {path, op:'add'|'remove', event, dryRun, ...opfields}. For remove: address {event, groupIndex, hookIndex} + expected {command} — server re-parses the RAW file, verifies the addressed entry still matches expected (else 409, like apply-fix preconditions). For add: {event, matcher?, hook:{type:'command', command}} appended per the same serialization rules the client-side hooks/logic.ts addHookToSettings uses today (read it; keep semantics aligned). Path resolves through resolveWriteTarget with the EXISTING scopes (global dirs are already write scopes — no allowlist change); O_NOFOLLOW discipline via the existing write primitives; deletes-to-trash not applicable (file edit). Serialization: parse raw JSON, mutate hooks block only, JSON.stringify(,null,2)+newline (document formatting normalization). dryRun:true returns the REDACTED unified diff (reuse the existing /api/write diff+redaction machinery in src/server/write.ts+diff.ts — raw content must never reach the wire, per fix-patch-carries-content). dryRun:false writes atomically.

Response mirrors WriteResponse shape (pathScope included — client shows the global warning off it). TESTS: project + global fixture paths; redacted-file edit preserves the real secret bytes on disk (plant secret, remove a hook, assert secret intact + hook gone); 409 on address/expected mismatch and on absent hooks block; diff preview redacted (secret absent from wire); out-of-scope path 403 byte-identical; unauthorized 401; malformed JSON file → 400/409 clean error, file untouched. SECURITY REVIEW REQUIRED before close (new write surface).

Gates: direct binaries (tsc/eslint/prettier/vitest run src). Relates wmc.11 (do not close it — this is the hooks slice only).
acceptance_criteria: Structured op works on redacted global settings.json without secret loss; redacted diff; 409 preconditions; security tests; dedicated security review; gates green

- src/server/hooks-edit.ts (NEW): route + pure applyHookEdit/parseHookEditOp. Reuses commitResolved/statFile/readJsonBody/O_NOFOLLOW from write.ts, unifiedDiff from diff.ts, resolveWriteTarget, core redact/CAPS.

CONTRACT: POST /api/hooks/edit
 add:    {path, op:'add', event, matcher?, hook:{type,command}, dryRun?}
 remove: {path, op:'remove', address:{event,groupIndex,hookIndex}, expected:{command}, dryRun?}
 dryRun defaults true (dryRun!==false). Response mirrors WriteResponse:
 dry-run: {diff, willCreate:false, willModify:true, pathScope}
 commit:  {committed:true, created:false, modified:true, path, pathScope, diff}
 diff is REDACTED before serialization (raw never on wire). Errors: 400 bad body/op/over-cap result; 403 out-of-scope/non-config/symlink (byte-identical, no oracle); 404 in-scope absent file (edit needs an existing file); 409 {error:'conflict'} preconditions (malformed JSON file, root/hooks not object, non-array event on add, address gone, expected.command mismatch) — file untouched; 413 on-disk file over 64KiB.

DECISIONS: addressing + add/remove/prune semantics match web/src/pages/hooks/logic.ts (parseHooksBlock coords; add appends NEW group, blank matcher omitted; remove prunes empty group/event/hooks block). Divergence (documented): add 409s instead of silently clobbering a non-object hooks / non-array event (client only reaches add after parseHooksBlock ok). Formatting normalization documented: whole file re-serialized JSON.stringify(root,null,2)+'\n'. Read path uses O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW (ELOOP→403); write via commitResolved (the one guarded primitive). File-must-exist → 404 (create flows keep using /api/write — nothing redacted to protect there).

TESTS: dry-run no-disk-touch (mtime+bytes); add append/event-create/block-create/blank-matcher; remove keep-sibling/prune-all; CORE SECURITY: global fixture with planted sk- secret in env → remove via absolute global path → on-disk secret bytes intact, hooks block pruned, wire (JSON.stringify of response) free of secret, diff contains [REDACTED: (env context lines redacted), pathScope:'global'; all 409s file-untouched; 403 existing-vs-missing byte-identical; symlink leaf 403; 404; 413; 401 no-token; 403 CSRF; 12 malformed-body 400s.

title: Terminal panel overlays every page: [hidden] defeated by .terminal-page{display:flex}
description:
Follow-up to agentconfig-4a3 live testing. The shell mounts <Terminal> persistently on every route (App.tsx ~line 208, ngs.2 design: tabs + live PTYs survive navigation) and hides it off-route with the HTML hidden attribute (Terminal.tsx:248). But terminal.css sets .terminal-page{display:flex} — an author display rule always beats the UA stylesheet's [hidden]{display:none} in the cascade — so the terminal <main> renders on EVERY route. Both mains share grid-area:main (styles/grid.css), so the terminal (its 'Terminal' heading, [+ZSH]/[+CLAUDE]/[+CODEX] tab bar, and giant NO SIGNAL empty state) draws transparently on top of the active page. Confirmed via headless-Chrome screenshot on #/ (Overview). Functionality is unaffected; it is a pure paint/stacking bug.

FIX: restate the hidden semantics at author level in terminal.css: .terminal-page[hidden]{display:none}. 

VERIFY: screenshots — (1) Overview shows no terminal bleed-through; (2) #/terminal still renders the terminal page normally; (3) navigate away and back — tabs survive (persistent mount untouched).

title: settings-local-committed emits create-file fix for existing .gitignore (should append)
description: Found during wmc.1: the scanner doesn't COLLECT .gitignore, so the settings-local-committed analyzer can't see an existing one and emits a create-file fix whose patch is the whole file body. Proper fix: collect .gitignore in the scanner (like np8.12/np8.13 additive KNOWN_FILES) so the analyzer sees existing content and emits a replace-file fix that APPENDS the ignore line (preserving existing content). src/core work. Until then the 409 guard prevents data loss but the .gitignore fix no-ops on existing files.
